TIME WARPING WITH HELLINGER ELASTICITY
YULY BILLIG
Abstract.We consider a matching problem for time series with
values in an arbitrary metric space, with the stretching penalty
given by the Hellinger kernel. To optimize this matching, we in-
troduce the Elastic Time Warping algorithm with a cubic compu-
tational complexity.
1.Introduction
Functional data analysis has a multitude of applications: speech
recognition [10], biomedical [7], motion analysis [14], economics [9],
DNA matching [5], to name a few.

The paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we discuss the prop-
erties of the Hellinger metric on the group of diffeomorphisms. In
Section 3, we use the metric on diffeomorphisms to define a metric on
the space of functions with the Hellinger penalty for stretching. Fi-
nally, in Section 4, we introduce the Elastic Time Warping algorithm
that optimizes matching between two time series, based on a similarity
coefficient with the Hellinger kernel.

structure.title: Introduction
structure.summary: This document introduces a new time warping algorithm called "Elastic Time Warping" that uses Hellinger elasticity for matching time series. The core contribution is a novel similarity coefficient that can be applied to time series with values in arbitrary metric spaces, unlike previous methods limited to vector spaces. This coefficient incorporates a penalty for stretching time, defined using the Hellinger distance on the group of diffeomorphisms. The paper outlines the mathematical framework, including the Hellinger metric on diffeomorphisms and its application to define a metric on function spaces. Finally, it presents the Elastic Time Warping algorithm, detailing its computational complexity and memory requirements, and discusses its potential applications in areas like functional data analysis and DNA matching.

structure.title: Hellinger metric on Diff([0,1]).
structure.summary:
The document introduces the concept of "Time Warping with Hellinger Elasticity." It outlines the paper's structure, which includes discussing the properties of the Hellinger metric on diffeomorphisms, defining a metric on function spaces with a Hellinger penalty for stretching, and finally presenting the Elastic Time Warping algorithm for optimizing time series matching.

Section 2 focuses on the Hellinger metric on the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the segment [0,1]. It defines the Hellinger similarity coefficient and explores its variants, such as the Hellinger distance, demonstrating that these variants also satisfy the properties of a distance function. A key property discussed is the invariance of the Hellinger similarity coefficient under reparametrizations, leading to right-invariant metrics.

Section 3 extends this concept to define a distance on the space of bounded functions. It introduces a new distance function that incorporates a penalty for stretching, using the Hellinger distance between diffeomorphisms. This new distance is shown to be a metric and is compared to existing metrics like the Skorohod metric. The section also highlights the invariance of this new distance under reparametrizations.

structure.title: Distance on the space of functions with a Hellinger penalty for stretching
structure.summary: This document introduces a new distance metric called "Hellinger Elasticity" for time series, which penalizes stretching in time using a Hellinger distance term. It defines this metric and proves it is a valid metric. The document then introduces a similarity coefficient, K(f, g), which is a decreasing function of the distance and is useful for applications where closeness is more important than distance. It also outlines an Elastic Time Warping algorithm for computing this similarity coefficient, detailing its recurrence relations and computational complexity. The algorithm is based on dynamic programming and aims to find an optimal time warping that maximizes the similarity.
